newsitem.title: USA: Downgrades won't derail Norfolk Southern debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Downgrades won't derail Norfolk Southern debt deal.

text.p: A multi-notch downgrade to Norfolk Southern Corp's debt by two rating agencies should not adversely impact the firm's upcoming debt offering, syndicate sources said.

"With the size of the (Conrail Inc) accquisition we expected the ratings to go down this far...it's not a surprise," said one market source."The sentiment was that they had excellent ratings but over-rated for that industry."
On Tuesday, Standard & Poor's issued a four-notch downgrade to Norfolk Southern's senior secured and unsecured debt ratings, to BBB-plus from AA-minus.
Later, Moody's cut Norfolk Southern's senior unsecured debt by three notches to Baa1 from A1.

The actions reflected the financial impact of approximately $6.0 billion of acquistion debt to fund Norfolk Southern's 58 percent share of the joint Norfolk Southern/CSX Corp (42 percent) tender offer, for the assets of Conrail Inc, the rating agencies said.
"A similar thing happened with CSX...by the time the deal was launched it was already factored in," said another syndicate source.
Last week, CSX Corp successfully issued a $2.5 billion multi-tranche debt offering despite a downgrade to the company's ratings by Moody's and S&P.
CSX Corp's senior unsecured debt is rated BBB by Standard & Poor's and Baa2 by Moody's.
Meanwhile, Norfolk Southern's upcoming offering is expected to consist of between $3.0 to $4.0 billion of multi-tranche debt, sources said.

The deal, currently in roadshow, is rumored to include a five-year issue, a 10-year issue, a 30-year issue with a make-whole call, and a 40-year maturity, putable in the seventh year, market sources said.
JP Morgan Securites and Merrill Lynch & Co are expected to jointly underwrite the deal, sources said.
